items.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021
items.q: when I play “Laura” I think of Gene Tierney and Clifton Webb and the movies

ctx.x: You will be adding a nice element to our collection. And I’m wondering as you play a piece like that, or your own compositions, and you’re sort of in the middle of it, do you ever surprise yourself by where your hands go and the sounds that are created?

Yes I do. I’m only semi-conscious at the time because when I play “Laura” I think of Gene Tierney and Clifton Webb and the movies, so there are a lot of different plot things when I do the Theodorakis [inaudible] I think of the coup d’état in Greece in 1967, so their imageries, and they almost overpower me. And sometimes that’s why I like to play alone or a duo, because the plots and the characters come right to me. It’s very hard to

subtly be present and aware. I do hear some things back but there are so many CDs I haven’t heard of other people and DVDs of film noir. But I think I am surprised. I like to modulate. I don’t plan that but my hands seem to like that.
